title: A projective modification of a reduced proper scheme
statement:
Let $S$ be affine Noetherian and $X\to S$
proper, with $X$ reduced.
There are a proper map $\pi:Y\to X$ and a dense open $U\subset X$
such that $\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism and $Y\to S$ is
projective.

proof.text: Write $f:X\to S$ for the given proper morphism. By [def-weil-proper-morphism], $f$ is separated and of finite type. The base $S$ is Noetherian, so [lem-weil-pbc-chow-noetherian] applies. Choose the data in its existential conclusion: an integer $N\geq0$, a scheme $Y$, a proper surjective map $\pi:Y\to X$, an immersion $i:Y\to\mathbf P^N_S$ over $S$, and a dense open $U\subseteq X$ with $\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ an isomorphism. The relation $p\circ i=f\circ\pi$, with $p:\mathbf P^N_S\to S$, is part of the cited statement.

By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition], $h=f\circ\pi:Y\to S$ is proper. The structural morphism $p:\mathbf P^N_S\to S$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], applied to the finite coordinate set $\{0,\ldots,N\}$, and therefore separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated] with source $Y$, target $\mathbf P^N_S$, base $S$, proper structure morphism $h$, and morphism $i$; the required equality $p\circ i=h$ is supplied by step 1. Thus $i$ is proper. It is already an immersion, so [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed] makes $i$ a closed immersion. This uses only the stated properties of the chosen data, without identifying it with another construction.

proof.text: The proper structure morphism $h=f\circ\pi$ from step 2 is of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], hence quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The closed immersion $i:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_S$ from step 2 satisfies $p\circ i=h$ by step 1, and $N\geq0$. It therefore witnesses H-projectivity of $h$; together with quasi-compactness this is precisely projectivity in [def-pc-projective-morphism]. The proper $\pi$ and dense-open isomorphism of step 1 give the remaining conclusions.
